Integrate the second derivative $f''(x) = (4x + 1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ with respect to $x$:
$$f'(x) = \int (4x + 1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\,dx = \frac{(4x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{\frac{1}{2} \times 4} + c = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4x + 1} + c$$

Since $f$ has a stationary minimum at $x = 2$, $f'(2) = 0$:
$$f'(2) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4(2) + 1} + c = 0 \implies \frac{1}{2}(3) + c = 0 \implies c = -\frac{3}{2}$$
$$f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4x + 1} - \frac{3}{2}$$

In an arithmetic progression, the common difference $d$ is constant:
$$d = T_2 - T_1 = -1 - 1 = -2$$

Calculate the third term $T_3 = f(0)$:
$$f(0) = T_2 + d = -1 + (-2) = -3$$

Integrate $f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}} - \frac{3}{2}$ with respect to $x$:
$$f(x) = \int \left(\frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{\frac{1}{2}} - \frac{3}{2}\right) dx = \frac{\frac{1}{2}(4x + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} - \frac{3}{2}x + k = \frac{1}{12}(4x + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{3}{2}x + k$$

Use the initial condition $f(0) = -3$ from part (ii) to find $k$:
$$-3 = \frac{1}{12}(4(0) + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{3}{2}(0) + k = \frac{1}{12} + k \implies k = -3 - \frac{1}{12} = -\frac{37}{12}$$
$$f(x) = \frac{1}{12}(4x + 1)^{\frac{3}{2}} - \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{37}{12}$$
